summary: SCIM bulk import Unicode bulkId normalization causes duplicate user records and orphaned role bindings in private deployment
description: Issue summary: After a scheduled SCIM bulk import of ~4k users from FinSight's identity provider into their private Redwood deployment, many end users reported missing role assignments and consequent 403s when attempting admin actions. Investigation shows duplicate SCIM user resources were created for a subset of accounts. Impact: ~120 users lost access to role-bound features (admin and billing consoles) for affected tenant. This blocks day-to-day ops for those users and is high-impact for the customer's compliance workflows. Environment: Private deployment in us-east-1 connecting to customer IdP over a proxy. SCIM ingestion service runs on dedicated tenant pool. Temporary workaround requested by customer to restore admin access quickly.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a SCIM 2.0 bulk request to /scim/v2/Bulk with entries containing 'bulkId' fields that include non-ASCII characters (accented letters and emoji in FinSight test data)
2) POST the bulk payload to customer's private Redwood SCIM endpoint through the same proxy path used in production
3) Observe 201 responses but inspect returned 'id' values for duplicated email local-parts mapped to different resource ids
4) Attempt login for duplicated user; auth succeeds but RBAC lookup uses new resource id which has no role bindings => 403 on admin routes

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Duplicate user resources created when the combination of client payload bulkId and transformations performed by the customer's proxy + our normalizer produced two different canonical forms, bypassing our dedupe check which relies on exact match of externalId or externalIdHash.

Reproduction: Performed a local bulk import passing identical logical bulkId strings but toggled header 'Content-Type: application/scim+json; charset=utf-8' vs 'application/json' and observed different normalized values saved in resource.externalId. Repro reproducible with payload containing non-ASCII chars (accented characters and emoji).

Root cause (interim): Our SCIM ingestion path performs normalization but does not apply a stable canonicalization before dedupe; an upstream proxy in the customer's network was re-encoding bytes which led to two different bytes sequences across retries; the second create succeeded and returned a new ID rather than treating as idempotent retry.
Related artifacts: linked internal ticket INT-1289 tracking code changes; reproduced with test payload stored in private S3 at s3://redwood-dev-repro/974206-payload.json (internal access only).
Risk assessment: Medium-high for bulk imports that include non-ASCII characters. Not expected to affect customers who use ASCII-only bulkIds.
related_github_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6218 (proposed: scim: add bulkId NFC normalization and idempotency-key support)
resolution: Workaround applied: Ran reconciliation script that finds duplicate users by matching on verified email claim and merges role bindings from orphaned resource ids into canonical resource. Script run completed 2026-03-13 04:20 UTC. Restored access for 118/120 affected users; two users required manual audit due to email aliases.

Short-term mitigation: For the customer's tenant, enabled a middleware normalization flag to canonicalize incoming SCIM bulkId strings to NFKC and to compute externalIdHash prior to persistence. This is a runtime toggle and will be removed after permanent fix.

Permanent fix plan: INT-1289 implements deterministic canonicalization (NFC) at the SCIM gateway and adds an idempotency-key header support for bulk requests plus stronger dedupe checks (email + externalId canonical match). Target PR merged and under test; rollout planned to production on 2026-03-21 behind a feature flag.

Follow-ups: 1) Post-incident runbook addition describing checks to run after bulk imports. 2) Add test vectors with non-ASCII bulkIds to CI for scim ingestion. 3) Customer education doc to recommend avoiding emoji in bulkId and to use stable ASCII identifiers where possible.
Status: In Progress. Customer restored to acceptable state; permanent fix in QA and tentatively scheduled for controlled rollout.
